s: PostgreSQL, MySQL, joins, indexing, transactions, normalization
d: Relational databases are the backbone of most applications. SQL knowledge — joins, indexes, transactions, normalization — is non-negotiable. PostgreSQL is the gold standard for new projects.
c: SQL: SELECT JOIN WHERE GROUP BY HAVING ORDER BY

p: Relational Databases store data in tables with predefined schemas. They use SQL (Structured Query Language) and guarantee ACID properties (Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability) for reliable transactions.
1. Define strict schema using DDL (CREATE TABLE).
2. Ensure relationships using Primary and Foreign Keys.
3. Maintain data integrity via constraints (UNIQUE, NOT NULL).

SELECT Users.Name, Posts.Title 
FROM Users 
JOIN Posts ON Users.ID = Posts.User_ID 
WHERE Users.Role = 'Admin';

[Users Table]          [Posts Table]

----------------       --------------------
